answer:
Record the maker as one collective actor: an instance of E74 Group standing for the women of the named extended-family household, attached to the basket's E12 Production by P14 carried out by. Do not name the three later-identified women as the makers, and do not retreat to a bare E39 Actor. The three women belong on the same event, but held at P11 had participant, and the identification that produced their names belongs in an E13 Attribute Assignment of its own.

First, note that the CRM gives you no direct property from an object to its maker. `connect E22 E74` and `connect E24 E39` return only ownership, custody, rights and depiction paths (each expanded as a full path through E8 Acquisition or E10 Transfer of Custody). The maker is expressible only as the actor of the production event: E12 Production, P108 has produced the basket, P14 carried out by the actor. So the class choice you are asking about is really a choice about what you attach to that one event, and the CRM says as much in general terms - its expressive power is described as coming not from classifying entities but from documenting their interrelation through well-defined properties.

Why E74 Group and not three instances of E21 Person. P14 carried out by is a subproperty of P11 and its scope note says it implies causal or legal responsibility. The consultation explicitly could not confirm which of the three women, if any, handled this particular basket, so attaching any of them by P14 would assert exactly the responsibility your record denies. The field diary, by contrast, does attest a collective agent: the women of one household, working together in one session, under their senior weaver. E74's scope note fits this without stretching - a gathering of people becomes an instance of E74 Group when it exhibits organisational characteristics typified by actions performed together, and families are named in the same scope note as particular examples of E74 Group. Nothing in E74 requires the group to be formal, incorporated, or even named: the SIG considered narrowing it that way (Pat Riva's proposal in t1085 would have required 'any named gatherings or organizations of two or more people'), and at the 41st joint meeting decided instead to leave E74 broad and put the narrower LRM notion in LRMoo as a separate subclass. Give the group P1 is identified by with the household appellation the diary records, and P2 has type with a term such as 'extended-family household weaving group'.

Why not a bare E39 Actor. E39 is instantiable, but it records only that some responsible agent existed, which is less than your source actually says. It also costs you structure: P107 has current or former member is declared on E74, not on E39 - compare the outgoing property lists of the two concepts - so an E39 placeholder could never carry membership if you later learn it. Instantiating E39 directly is the right move only when you genuinely cannot tell whether an individual or a collective was responsible. Here you can tell, so the vaguer class throws away evidence you hold.

Where the three named women go. Make each an E21 Person and attach them to the production event by P11 had participant, not by P14. P11 covers active or passive participation and its scope note states that the property implies the actor was involved but does not imply any causal relationship. That is precisely the claim the consultation supports (present and working that day) without the claim it withholds (made this basket). E12's scope note allows a production to be collective - 'the printing of a thousand books, for example, would normally be considered a single event' - so the cleanest shape is a single E12 for the communal work session, P108 has produced this basket (and any siblings of it), P14 carried out by the household women's group, P11 had participant the three named persons. If you need a narrower event for this basket alone, nest it inside the session with P9 consists of and keep the women's P11 on the session, not on the narrower production. Note also that P11's scope note holds that collective actors participate physically only via their representing persons, which is consistent with this split: the group bears the responsibility, the identified individuals are the physical participants.

Record the consultation itself, rather than absorbing its output as fact. The specification's Authorship of Knowledge Base Contents principle treats unattributed statements as the maintaining institution's own view, and directs that statements which carry their own authorship be expressed as knowledge-creation events. So: an E13 Attribute Assignment for the community consultation, P14 carried out by the consulting community body (itself an E74 Group), P4 has time-span for when it happened, P140 assigned attribute to the E12 Production, P141 assigned each of the three E21 Persons, and P177 assigned property of type a term for P11 had participant. This leaves the museum neutral on the identification, names who made it and when, and keeps it distinguishable from the diary's own attribution.

The senior weaver. She is a real individual known only by role, which E21 Person admits (persons who live or are assumed to have lived; no name is required, only an identifiable individual). Give her P1 is identified by an appellation such as 'senior weaver of household X', and attach her to the production by P14 carried out by with P14.1 in the role of a term for her guiding role - the same construction as P14's own worked example, Michelangelo in the role of master craftsman. That is a genuine P14: the diary does assert her responsibility for the work.

Two things to avoid. Do not assert P107 has current or former member between the three named women and the household group: your sources say they were present and working, not that they belong to that household. Use P107 only for membership the record actually establishes. And do not let the weaving cooperative the basket was collected from slide into the maker slot - it is the point of collection, a different actor in a different event.

Finally, for honesty about the model's limits: the SIG's own attempt to give this exact situation a dedicated property failed. Robert Sanderson raised it as Issue 542 in t1477, with the 'workshop of Rembrandt' case that is the same shape as yours - we know some members of the group did it but not which, and not all of them - and proposed a subproperty of P14 meaning 'carried out by member or members of'. The issue was made dependent on CRMsoc, and was closed in April 2025 without any new property when the SIG discontinued CRMsoc. So P14 to the Group with the individuals held at P11 is not a workaround around a missing feature; it is the answer CRMbase currently offers, and the finer distinction you might want (that only some unidentified members of the group did the work) is not expressible in CRMbase and should go in P3 has note if it matters to your readers.

rejected_alternatives.option: E39 Actor instantiated directly, as the 'broader, unspecified kind of actor'
rejected_alternatives.why_not: It records only that some responsible agent existed, which is less than the field diary establishes. It also blocks structure you may need later: P107 has current or former member is declared on E74 Group, not on E39 Actor, so an E39 placeholder can never carry membership. Direct instantiation of E39 is warranted only where you cannot tell individual from collective; here the diary tells you it was a collective.

rejected_alternatives.option: The three named women as makers, i.e. three E21 Persons on P14 carried out by
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P14 carried out by implies causal or legal responsibility per its scope note, and the consultation could not confirm which of the three, if any, handled this basket. This would assert precisely what the record denies. They belong on P11 had participant, which explicitly does not imply a causal relationship.

rejected_alternatives.option: The weaving cooperative as the E74 Group that made it
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The cooperative is where the basket was collected in the 1970s, not what the diary names as the maker. It belongs to the acquisition/custody side (E8 Acquisition or E10 Transfer of Custody, which is what connect E22 E74 actually returns), not to the production event.

rejected_alternatives.option: E66 Formation for the household group
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Nothing in the record documents a formation event for an extended-family household. Instantiating E66 would invent an event to justify the group, and E74 needs no formation event to be instantiated.

rejected_alternatives.option: I2 Belief (CRMinf) on the identification of the three women
rejected_alternatives.why_not: It would let you record a graded belief value on the attribution, but nothing here needs it: E13 Attribute Assignment names the asserting body and date, and simply not asserting P14 for the individuals already carries the 'if any' uncertainty under the open-world reading. Adding an extension model here is machinery beyond the evidence.

rejected_alternatives.option: A dedicated 'carried out by member or members of' subproperty of P14
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Proposed by Robert Sanderson and tracked as Issue 542, made dependent on CRMsoc, and closed in April 2025 without a new property when CRMsoc was discontinued. It does not exist, so it cannot be recommended.

siblings_considered.why_not: E21 Person is E74's only sibling under E39 Actor, and it is the rival the case is built around. It is ruled out for the maker slot because using it there means attaching a named individual by P14 carried out by, which implies causal responsibility that the community consultation explicitly could not establish for any of the three women. The evidence for who made the basket is evidence about a collective, so the collective class is the one it supports.

For the three consultation-identified women and the senior weaver, E74 Group is wrong in the other direction: each is attested as a distinct individual, and no source claims the three of them constituted a unit that acted collectively. E74 would require organisational characteristics or actions performed together, which is asserted of the household's women, not of the trio the consultation happened to be able to name.

E65 Creation is a sibling under E63 Beginning of Existence and covers conceptual or immaterial products. A coiled basket is a physical human-made thing brought into existence by material work, so the modification-of-matter branch applies; E65 would also fail to support P108 has produced, which is the property that anchors the maker to this object.

E87 Curation Activity is a sibling under E7 Activity and is tempting for a museum-run community consultation, but its scope is the management and preservation of an E78 Curated Holding under a curation plan. What has to be recorded here is one specific assertion about one specific relation - which persons participated in this production - and only E13 carries P140 assigned attribute to, P141 assigned and P177 assigned property of type to express that assertion and hold the museum neutral about it.

notes: Two friction points with the tools. (1) `quote` only accepts thread, message, episode or document chunk ids; passing a concept id such as P11 fails with 'unknown source id'. Nothing in the visible output of `concept` or `docs` shows a chunk id, so I had to re-run `docs ... --json` to learn the form (crm732#P11, crm732#s0046, minutes:<doc>#s016) before any scope-note phrase could be verified. Worth surfacing chunk ids in the human-readable `docs` output. (2) The siblings block of `concept E13` lists the other subclasses of E7 Activity but not E13's own subclasses (E14, E15, E16, E17), which are the classes a reader is most likely to be choosing among when they reach E13; I had to infer their existence from elsewhere in the output. Substantively I found no argument against E74 here: the SIG's one recorded attempt to sharpen this exact case (Issue 542) died with CRMsoc rather than being resolved, and the 41st-meeting decision on Issue 371 deliberately left E74 broad enough to cover an informal household collective. I did not claim E21 and E74 are formally disjoint - the specification's Disjointness section declares only E2/E77 and E18/E28 and says explicitly that no comprehensive list of disjoint pairs is provided.
